# ListenerRadius <img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [3D Sound](Blitz3D-3D-Sound)

</div>


```blitzbasic
ListenerRadius:Void value:Float32, fade_ms:Int32=0
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | In | Float32 | required | The radius in units of the world. `0` (the default) is a point, as in the original. Below 0 is a runtime error. |
| `fade_ms` | In | Int32 | `0` | How many milliseconds it takes to get to the new value. `0` (the default) changes it at once. Below 0 is a runtime error. |

## Description

<img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14"> This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Makes the listener a ball instead of a point, so that a sound that passes close by moves from one speaker to the other and changes its pitch over a moment instead of all at once. This is a BlitzLLVM extension.

## Differences

* The radius is added to the one of the sound ([ChannelRadius](ChannelRadius)). The panning and the doppler speeds then use the direction divided by the square root of distance² + radius² instead of the distance, so they are weaker close by and the same as before far away. The volume does not change with the radius. [GetListenerRadius](GetListenerRadius) tells the value.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
; The player is a ship of about 4 units across.
ListenerRadius 2
```
